program.how: written for ounce-core from the paper's definition (section 2) and FIPS 197 AES-128 (S-box computed by GF(2^8) inversion, not tabulated); Poly1305 arithmetic mod 2^130-5 in five 26-bit limbs. No third-party code copied. The chain driver re-implements, in the program's own words, the short key/nonce/message feedback procedure that the author's test-poly1305aes.c uses to generate its output (the test source was read to learn the procedure, not copied)
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: the four examples of the paper's Appendix B (messages of 2, 0, 32 and 63 bytes) reproduce: the polynomial value m(r) mod 2^130-5, AES_k(n) and the 16-byte authenticator (12 of 12 values)
400 AES-128 known answers (NIST Monte Carlo keys and plaintexts, as printed by the author's test-aes.out) reproduce (400 of 400)

a chain of 10010 Poly1305-AES authenticators (message lengths 0 to 1000, ten rounds; each authenticator feeds the next key, nonce and message) is computed and 1001 of them (every tenth; each depends on all earlier ones) equal the published test-poly1305aes.out lines (1001 of 1001)

expected_values_source.what: Appendix B examples parsed mechanically from the text of the fetched paper PDF; AES vectors and authenticators parsed from the author's published test outputs test-aes.out and test-poly1305aes.out (first 10010 lines, which the author's page says are the expected output)
expected_values_source.note: the vectors are data, copied as numbers; none of the author's code was copied

negative_control: built with -DCLAMP_R3=31 (r[3] masked with 31 instead of 15), the 12 example values and 400 AES answers still match (their r[3] is below 16) but only 1 of 1001 chain values matches and the program exits 1; built with -DAES_ROUNDS=9, 4 of 12 example values, 0 of 400 AES and 0 of 1001 chain values match and the program exits 1
not_checked: the paper's security bound (at most 14*D*ceil(L/16)/2^106) or any cryptanalysis
the 8,990 chain authenticators not compared one-by-one (they are covered only through the chain dependency) and the published md5 checksums of the longer outputs
speed figures (the paper's Athlon cycle counts say nothing about emulator run time)
AES-192/256 and Poly1305 with other ciphers; the later Poly1305 variants (ChaCha20-Poly1305) are a separate check
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces the paper's Appendix B values and the author's published test outputs for the inputs listed. It does not show the MAC is secure.
